question: An engineer is running several Claude Code sessions in parallel from the same project directory, using claude -p for automation. They capture the session ID from one run's JSON output and later want to resume that exact session with a follow-up prompt, from the same directory. Which command does this correctly?
options: A) claude --continue "<follow-up prompt>", since --continue always resumes the exact session ID most recently captured from JSON output.
B) claude -p --resume <session-id> "<follow-up prompt>", run from the same project directory the original session started in.
C) claude -p "<follow-up prompt>" --session-id <session-id>, which starts a new session but forces it to reuse the given identifier.
D) claude --resume with no arguments, then selecting the session from the interactive picker, since -p sessions are listed there by session ID.
correct_answers: B) claude -p --resume <session-id> "<follow-up prompt>", run from the same project directory the original session started in.
explanations: Incorrect. --continue resumes the most recent session in the directory, not a specific captured session ID, so it could resume the wrong session if others have run since.

Correct. Passing the captured session ID to --resume under -p sends a follow-up prompt to that exact session; lookup is scoped to the project directory and its worktrees, so the command must run from there.
Incorrect. There is no --session-id flag for forcing a new session to adopt an existing identifier; --resume is the mechanism for continuing a specific session.
Incorrect. Sessions created with claude -p do not appear in the interactive session picker; they can only be resumed by passing the session ID directly.
